k.label: AI Overview Clicks · bonus

i.label: AI Overview Impressions
i.hover: Example 1 — factor group:4% of searches showed no AI Overview.Example 2 — comparison group:8% of searches showed no AI Overview.What the percentage means:The example shows +50%: pages with the factor went without an AI Overview half as often. factors.factor: Money page links to at least five different external websites using followed links
factors.explanation:
Example setup:

example.com/seo-coach links to google.com, bing.com, schema.org, w3.org and mozilla.org. None of the five links has rel="nofollow".
What the row compares:

The money page links to at least five different external website addresses using links that are not marked rel="nofollow", compared with money pages that have no outgoing followed links to external websites. factors.factor: Semantic score 11 to 20 points over the Goldilocks zone
factors.explanation:
Example setup:

The top-10 competitors for the search average a semantic score of 55, so the Goldilocks zone is 50 to 60; the page scores 70, which is 15 points over the average.
What the row compares:

The semantic score is the SEO agent's keyword score: every word on the page is given a weight from the search's top-10 competitor pages (how often the competitors use it, and how relevant the word is to the search), the weights of all the words on the page are added up, and the page is ranked against every page on that search. The Goldilocks zone is the average score of the top-10 competitors. This row: pages whose score lands 11 to 20 points over that average, compared with pages more than 20 points under it. Measured September 7, 2026 on Google results 1 through 100 for 1,949 searches, 155,004 pages, whole-page text: 13,951 pages in this band versus 62,193 comparison pages. Placed in the AI Overview 6.29% versus 2.74%; Google positions 1 through 3 4.29% versus 2.21%; Google positions 1 through 5 7.21% versus 3.42%. This band is the best for reaching Google positions 1 through 5 and close to the best for AI Overview placement.

factors.factor: Named human author or reviewer

svt.label: SVT: Helps
svt.title:
Recorded example:
Over the same days the pages that kept the byline moved from an average Google position of 53.0 to 35.1, while the 10 pages without the byline moved from 57.7 to 42.0. The 5 pages Google recrawled on September 20 and 21 without the byline gained 3.9 places; the pages with the byline gained 26.5. The page /how-to-choose-seo-coach fell from position 17.2 to 66.1 the day after Google recrawled it without the byline. The byline stays, and an author already known in the same or a neighbouring field helps.

Source:
Live test on Josh's own website, September 2026: the author byline was removed from 10 pages and kept on the rest.

Open:
Click for the recorded result in the ledger.

factors.explanation:
Example:

“Written by Jane Smith.”

Pages visibly naming a human author or reviewer responsible for the content versus pages that do not. The percentages are the broad correlation across other people's websites, where the named author is usually unknown. A live test on Josh's own website in September 2026 says the opposite for a known author: the pages that kept the author byline moved from an average Google position of 53.0 to 35.1, the 10 pages that lost the byline moved from 57.7 to 42.0, the 5 pages recrawled without the byline on September 20 and 21 gained 3.9 places while the byline pages gained 26.5, and /how-to-choose-seo-coach fell from 17.2 to 66.1 the day after it was recrawled without the byline. Keep the byline when the author is already known in the same or a neighbouring field.

columns.label: Result order

Example order:
32.8%, 23.1%, 16.8%.

Sorting AI Overview citations from highest to lowest puts the largest citation percentage first.

columns.label: URL
columns.hover:

/seo-coach/

/top-pick/seo-coach/

Keep the main entity as the page name. For a second page, a folder states the purpose or claim. The wording-score table matches the tactics guide. A higher wording score is not a measured ranking or citation gain, and no score establishes that the second-page URL avoids a ranking drop.

20 of every 100 measured pages using the setup reached Google positions 1–5.

get_tactics.title: AI SEO Complete Ranking Tactics (Tested and proven)
get_tactics.text:
AI Overview tactics — rules and supporting results

Student guide · 3 September 2026

## AI Overview tactics

Protect page-one Google visibility while improving the chance that an AI Overview cites the money page.

Hover over or tap Why this rule to see the supporting results, competing results and exact report rows. Examples illustrate the wording or setup; invented names and numbers are not real business claims. When increasing amounts of the same factor produce progressively worse results, the practical rule stops before the first questionable amount; every still-higher amount does not need a separate test.

Yellow text includes the September 25 additions and the September 28 daily branded short-video tactic (rule 15c).

Open the correlation report ↗ (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzIzhQNAgAvascAR5-YaT-aWaUCrkEHzIQniCQUKHDlH4wlFnkMJckC6tIOSp9CUFHsZw/exec)Open the manual tests ↗ (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html)Download the matching PDF ↗ (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/ai_overview_tactics.pdf)Show all explanationsPrint / save as PDF

Content (#content)Naming spots (#naming)Structure (#structure)Links (#links)Commercial pages (#commercial)

## Content that gives Google an answer

## 01Name the thing, state the fact, and make the connection explicit.

Write checkable details about named products, people, places or services: measurements, prices, dates, requirements and observed results, instead of an unsupported claim that an option is excellent. Aim for at least 8 out of 10 on named entity fact binding, specific observed detail, authority evidence, technical feature to use case binding, verifiable facts and numbers, and facts presented like a specification sheet.

Name the source, qualification, document or method behind every important claim. Attach each technical feature to the situation where that feature matters. Lay the attributes out like a specification sheet — model, price, duration, requirement — rather than as adjectives.

Example:
“North College's SEO coaching course includes 12 lessons over six weeks and costs $300. The published course outline lists 30 teaching hours. Each recorded lesson stays available for 12 months, which suits shift workers who cannot attend live.”

Why this rule

Named entity fact binding: +142% citations; +60% AI Overview clicks; +110% top-three rankings; +83% top-five rankings.

Authority evidence: +124% citations; +106% AI Overview clicks; +49% top-three rankings; +66% top-five rankings.

Specific observed detail: +116% citations; +98% AI Overview clicks; +46% top-three rankings; +41% top-five rankings.

Verifiable facts and numbers scored 9 or 10: +100% citations; +63% AI Overview clicks; +39% top-five rankings.

Technical feature to use case binding: +60% citations; +44% AI Overview clicks; +5% top-five rankings.

Verifiable facts and numbers: +56% citations; +101% AI Overview clicks; +15% top-five rankings.

Facts presented like a specification sheet (score 8-10): +51% citations; +14% AI Overview clicks; +46% top-five rankings.

Manual Search 43 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-43) also put the page scoring 10 out of 10 for checkable facts first. View the answer screenshot. (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/screenshots/SEARCH-43-ai-mode.png)

## 02Explain which option fits which situation, including the important limitation.

Answer the decision the searcher has to make. Aim for at least 8 out of 10 on crucial non-obvious information, contextual option fit, decision guidance, option set coverage, answers likely next questions, limitations and edge cases, prevents likely misunderstandings, and tradeoff explanation.

Name the meaningful alternatives, say which named alternative fits which situation, answer the next question before the reader asks it, state the exceptions and the conditions that change the answer, and clear up the confusion the reader is likely to have. Explain the benefit-versus-cost relationship in ordinary sentences. Do not label a heading or section “Pros and cons”.

Example:
“North College’s group course costs $300 plus a compulsory $80 exam fee: $380 total. South College’s individual coaching costs $90 per hour and includes feedback on the learner’s own website.”

Why this rule

Crucial non-obvious information: +154% citations; +128% AI Overview clicks; +112% top-three rankings; +95% top-five rankings.

Contextual option fit: +115% citations; +191% AI Overview clicks; +19% top-five rankings.

Decision guidance: +108% citations; +187% AI Overview clicks; +45% top-three rankings; +30% top-five rankings.

Option set coverage: +86% citations; +134% AI Overview clicks; +13% top-five rankings.

Answers likely next questions (score 8-10): +74% citations; +156% AI Overview clicks; +5% top-five rankings.

Limitations and edge cases: +73% citations; +106% AI Overview clicks; +17% top-five rankings.

Prevents likely misunderstandings (score 8-10): +69% citations; +252% AI Overview clicks; −17% top-three rankings; +3% top-five rankings.

Tradeoff explanation: +45% citations; +70% AI Overview clicks; −22% top-three rankings; −14% top-five rankings.

## 03Use testing language only when an indexed third-party video shows the test.

Use “we tested”, “we measured”, “we found” or equivalent first-hand testing language only when an indexed YouTube or third-party video shows the claimed test and corroborates at least part of the facts and details stated on the money page. Without that video, drop the first-person testing claim and state only supported facts in third person.

Example with the required indexed video:
“We timed five Model A charging cycles; the average was 83 minutes.”
Example using a published source instead:
“The Model A manual lists a 90-minute charging time.”

Why this rule

Relies on self-asserted testing without a named method or concrete results: −5% citations; −3% AI Overview clicks; −32% top-three rankings; −47% top-five rankings.

First hand observation: +40% citations; +61% AI Overview clicks; +50% top-five rankings.

Has an embedded video or iframe: +53% citations; +31% AI Overview clicks; +47% top-five rankings.

Specific observed detail: +116% citations; +98% AI Overview clicks; +41% top-five rankings. These figures belong to the concrete-detail measurement, not to the video requirement.

Manual Search 37 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-37) placed the unsupported “we tested / we measured” page behind the other same-age pages. View the answer screenshot. (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/screenshots/SEARCH-37-ai-mode-partial.png)

## 04Start with a short factual answer containing the main entity.

Open with the direct answer or the decision-relevant fact, and name at least two concrete things with a specific fact about each. The opening paragraph is the one place to aim for 10 out of 10, on the direct answer and on the concrete named things. Keep the opening between 1 and 75 words and always under 120 words. Include the main entity phrase. Put the website's own business name in the first paragraph as one of the named things: the name the site uses for itself, not only “we” or “our”. Do not open with a question word, and do not address the reader as “you”.

Example:
“SEO coach Maya Reed teaches North College's six-week course, which includes 12 live lessons for $300.”
Named entities:
Maya Reed and North College, each with a specific detail. North College is the business that owns the page.
Same opening without the business name:
“Our SEO coach teaches this six-week course, which includes 12 live lessons for $300.”

Why this rule

Opening concrete entities: +82% citations; +94% AI Overview clicks; +56% top-three rankings; +47% top-five rankings.

Opening direct answer: +56% citations; +78% AI Overview clicks; +18% top-five rankings.

One short opening sentence with the main entity and concrete named things: +56% citations; +183% AI Overview clicks; +47% top-five rankings. That row measures four conditions together, including exactly one sentence under 45 words; the 45-word sentence is this row's own proof, not a separate requirement.

First paragraph opens with a question word: −20% citations; −61% top-three rankings; −47% top-five rankings.

First paragraph addresses the reader as you: −9% citations; −21% top-three rankings; −21% top-five rankings.

First paragraph 25 to 44 words: +11% citations; +20% AI Overview clicks; −8% top-five rankings.

First paragraph 45 to 69 words: +6% citations; −1% AI Overview clicks; +1% top-five rankings.

First paragraph under 25 words: −3% citations; +1% AI Overview clicks; +8% top-five rankings.

First paragraph 120 words or more: +25% citations; −36% AI Overview clicks; +58% top-three rankings; +21% top-five rankings.

First paragraph contains a number with a unit: +23% citations; −25% AI Overview clicks; −6% top-five rankings.

Business name in the first paragraph: +55% citations; +47% top-three rankings; +37% top-five rankings. Searches containing the business name itself are excluded from this row.

## Use the naming spots together

For “best seo coach”, the complete search phrase is “best seo coach”; the main entity is “seo coach”.

## 05Keep every naming spot on the same search topic.

The WINNER setup: cited by the AI Overview 32.8%, in the AI Overview's reference data 37.9%, Google positions 1–5 15.5%, on 58 pages from 56 websites. Search “best SEO coach”, main entity “SEO coach”.

Naming spot | What the winner does | Example for “best SEO coach” |

URL | Main entity phrase only | example.com/seo-coach |

Title tag | The EMQ first, inside a longer statement | Best SEO Coach for Small Businesses in 2026 |

Main heading (H1) | Main entity phrase inside a longer statement, worded differently from the title | Hire an SEO Coach Who Has Ranked 214 Teams |

Subheadings | Exactly one subheading carries the EMQ, once; no other subheading repeats it | H2: Why the Best SEO Coach Starts With Your Own Rankings |

Source: the WINNER row of the measured configuration table. (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzIzhQNAgAvascAR5-YaT-aWaUCrkEHzIQniCQUKHDlH4wlFnkMJckC6tIOSp9CUFHsZw/exec#emq-placement-table)

Single-variable tests on the CEG event pages that bear on the same case: a URL path under 30 characters helped; the searched phrase repeated three or more times in the page body helped; the searched phrase repeated three times across the domain and URL path helped; a URL two folders deep hurt; a title tag of 72 characters or more hurt; the phrase first appearing past 13,000 characters of the page source hurt.

URL example | How to use the example | Match to the search “best SEO coach” |

/best/seo-coach/ | Avoid in this setup. Contains every search word even with the folder separator; the higher wording score does not establish better rankings. | 0.864375 |

/top-pick/seo-coach/ | Prefer for naming a winner. Second-page advertorial naming the best SEO coach; no list required. | 0.823154 |

/toppick/seo-coach/ | Prefer the hyphenated version. Use /top-pick/seo-coach/; separating the words scored higher. | 0.811777 |

/recommendation/seo-coach/ | Use for a recommendation. Second page recommending an SEO coach. | 0.808751 |

/top-content/seo-coach/ | Use for a content-quality claim. Signals top-quality content about an SEO coach; a weaker match to “best SEO coach” than top-pick. | 0.805933 |

/seo-coach/ | Keep. Existing single money page; retain the main entity. | 0.798264 |

/comparison/seo-coach/ | Use for an actual comparison. Page comparing coaches; a weaker match to “best SEO coach” than top-pick. | 0.783110 |

/topcontent/seo-coach/ | Prefer the hyphenated version. Use /top-content/seo-coach/; separating the words scored higher. | 0.781654 |

/seo-coach/best/ | Avoid in this setup. Moving best after the page name still includes every search word. | Not measured |

/best-seo-coach/ | Avoid in this setup. Copies the complete search phrase into the page name. | Not measured |

/seo-coach-best/ | Avoid in this setup. Reordering the words still includes every search word. | Not measured |

/seo-coach-for-business/ | Avoid for this search. Changes the topic to coaching for businesses. | Not measured |

/seo-coach1/ | Not established. A number distinguishes the URL, but no saved result establishes that the number avoids a ranking drop. | Not measured |

/seo-coach-2026/ | Not established. A year distinguishes the URL, but no saved result establishes that the year avoids a ranking drop. | Not measured |

Choose the complete URL’s meaning, not one word in isolation. Higher scores mean a closer wording match to the search, not a measured ranking or citation gain.

Why this rule

URL wording: The table uses Google's gemini-embedding-001 search-retrieval setting, measured on 4 September 2026 using the exact paths, including slashes. All eight URL scores and the separate meaning comparisons. (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/tmp/url-token-scoring-20260904/gemini-url-token-scores.json)

Naming configuration: The recorded configuration (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzIzhQNAgAvascAR5-YaT-aWaUCrkEHzIQniCQUKHDlH4wlFnkMJckC6tIOSp9CUFHsZw/exec#aio-naming-winner) received 19 citations in 58 page/search observations from 56 websites (32.8%); complete-search-phrase URLs received 3 in 29 observations from 26 websites (10.3%) on different searches. Only three configuration paths contained nothing but the main entity, and none was cited; these groups do not establish the best exact URL or a ranking penalty for a synonym folder.

The recorded heading condition allowed H2 through H6; the teaching setup uses one H2. 58 configuration observations (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/tmp/url-naming-proof-20260903/recorded-58-winning-rows.json) · 29 comparison observations (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/tmp/url-naming-proof-20260903/recorded-29-comparison-rows.json).

## 06Put the complete search phrase in one H2, not several.

Keep the other subheadings specific to their sections and write statements, not questions. Reordering the search words does not remove repeated search words. Keep the main entity out of most subheadings.

One H2:
“Choosing the Best SEO Coach”
Other section headings:
“Course price”
“Lesson schedule”
“Tutor experience”

Why this rule

The report’s subheading instruction (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzIzhQNAgAvascAR5-YaT-aWaUCrkEHzIQniCQUKHDlH4wlFnkMJckC6tIOSp9CUFHsZw/exec#aio-naming-winner) favors one heading carrying the full search-word set: +21% citations, compared with −9% for multiple qualifying headings. The chosen setup uses one H2 and excludes question headings.

## 07Keep the answer on the same search topic as the title, URL and headings.

For “best SEO coach”, explain the coaching options and the facts that determine the choice. Do not narrow the whole page to businesses, a city or an industry unless that restriction is part of the search. Mention the actual subject naturally; do not add copies of the search phrase simply to meet a repetition count.

On-topic section heading:
“Comparing coaching fees”
On-topic sentence:
“North College charges $300 for six weeks; South College charges $220 for four weeks.”

Why this rule

Apply the chosen same-topic naming setup (#naming-setup) throughout the answer. This instruction does not prescribe a measured keyword-repetition quota.

## 08Keep the URL short and retain the main entity in the chosen naming-spot setup.

Do not interpret “short URL” as “remove every search word”. Two folders before the page name remain a manual-test risk even though the correlation result is positive.

Short URL:
 /seo-coach/
Two folders before the page name:
/services/coaching/seo-coach/

Why this rule

URL path contains fewer than 30 characters: −5% citations; +21% top-five rankings.

Two folders before the page name: +55% citations; +46% top-five rankings.

Manual Search 25 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-25) gave the two-folder page a source card while shorter-URL pages received inline links and facts.

## 10Use the real title tag, and keep the title under 72 characters.

Put the EMQ first in the actual title tag, followed by wording that stays on the same topic, and keep the whole title under 72 characters. Do not use a question or a different audience to lengthen the title.

Title:
“Best SEO Coach — Compare the Options”

Why this rule

Query in the real <title> tag, not a meta title: the laboratory result favors the actual title tag.

Title tag contains at least 72 characters: single-variable test, page mcuw, Manual Search 26 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-26): Google replaced the 72-plus-character title with the title of the embedded LED dance-floor page, on the search result and on the AI Overview citation card. That is the only tested reason for the length limit.

## Answer placement and page structure

## 11Put the answer near the beginning and inside as few enclosing page sections as practical.

Keep the essential answer before 13,000 characters of page content, and keep that answer inside few enclosing sections even when the rest of the layout is deeply nested. Do not put the answer after a long introduction or inside unnecessary nested sections.

Example opening answer:
“The event starts at 8 PM in Hall C. Admission costs $20.”

Why this rule

Answer sits directly off <body>, no wrappers: +96% citations in the laboratory comparison.

Answer sits shallower in the money page code than the competing page's answer: +40% citations.

Answer past 13,000 characters: −100% citations in the recorded laboratory comparison.

Average HTML nesting is at least 12.7 levels: +45% citations; +68% top-three rankings; +50% top-five rankings; −72% AI Overview clicks; −32% impressions. This row measures the whole page's average depth, not the answer's depth.

Manual Search 11 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-11) adds a negative result for the late-answer page and a positive result for the answer placed directly inside the page body.

## 12Grow the page to 2,100–2,500 useful words, the average of pages placed in the AI Overview, and keep the sentences standalone.

Expand the money page to between 2,100 and 2,500 main-content words by adding separate useful answers, never by padding an answer with irrelevant facts. Pages placed in the AI Overview or AI Mode answer average 2,312 words, the first and second sources it picks average 2,438 and 2,478 words, and pages at Google positions 1 through 5 average 2,174 to 2,539 words; pages at positions 51 through 100 average 1,083 to 1,922 words. Use specific numbers where the facts require numbers; do not add numbers to meet a quota. Keep 96 or more sentences between 8 and 30 words that do not start with it, they, this, that, these, those, he or she, and keep at least 80% of all sentences off those opening words. Start 30% to 45% of sentences with a name: the business, a person, a product, a place or a tool, written the way it is spelled with a capital letter. Each of those sentences must carry a fact about the name; a name with an adjective and no fact does nothing. Stop at 45%; beyond that the citation result falls back. Put body text inside paragraph tags rather than leaving text bare inside a div or a span.

Example sentence:
“North College’s course includes 12 live lessons and six weeks of tutor feedback.”
Three sentences, all starting with a name:
“North College charges $300 for the six-week course. Maya Reed teaches every lesson. Google Search Console shows the results.”
The same facts with no sentence starting with a name:
“The course costs $300 for six weeks. Every lesson is taught by the same tutor. The results show up in your dashboard.”
A name with no fact, which does not count:
“North College is the best choice for ambitious learners.”

Why this rule

2,500 to 3,500 main-content words: +20% citations; +38% AI Overview clicks; −12% top-five rankings.

5,000 or more main-content words: +26% citations; +70% AI Overview clicks; +14% top-five rankings.

Under 2,000 main-content words: −16% citations; −38% AI Overview clicks; +12% top-five rankings.

Under 1,000 main-content words: −13% citations; −53% AI Overview clicks; +8% top-five rankings.

At least 130 parsed sentences: +29% citations; +146% AI Overview clicks; −16% top-five rankings.

At least 96 sentences meet the mechanical standalone-sentence rule: +33% citations; +172% AI Overview clicks; −26% top-five rankings. The rule counts sentences of 8 to 30 words that do not begin with it, they, this, that, these, those, he or she.

At least 80% of sentences do not begin with a dependent pronoun: +17% citations; +186% AI Overview clicks; +43% top-three rankings; −8% top-five rankings.

Contains at least 27 separate numbers: +18% citations; +190% AI Overview clicks; −4% top-five rankings.

At least 1.2 numbers per 100 words: +15% citations; +147% AI Overview clicks; +1% top-five rankings.

Has answer text left bare inside a div or span: +10% citations; −37% AI Overview clicks; −17% impressions; −2% top-five rankings.

30% to 45% of sentences start with a name: +47% citations; +26% top-three rankings; +31% top-five rankings. Compared with pages under 20%.

More than 45% of sentences start with a name: +29% citations; +39% top-three rankings; +13% top-five rankings. Citations fall back from the 30% to 45% band.

Under 5% of sentences start with a name: −21% citations; −40% top-three rankings; −39% top-five rankings.

Names need facts attached. Split by the Named entity fact binding score, 30% to 45% of sentences starting with a name against under 20%: +1% citations at scores 1 to 3; +77% at scores 4 to 7; +37% at scores 8 to 10. Both groups average the same fact-binding score (6.8), so the two measurements are separate.

## More chances to answer precisely

More useful sections give the page more opportunities to answer the search precisely. Add each section for the answer it provides, not to reach a heading count.

Expand the money page by adding separate useful answers, each with the sections, numbers and images that answer needs. Use the extra length for distinct useful answers and images, not repetition or a word-count target by itself.

Add one to ten relevant images that clarify those answers. Do not add a section, an image or a fact that answers nothing.

Example:
A 2,400-word course page gives separate answers about price, eligibility, course length, lesson content and likely misunderstandings, with screenshots of the course outline and the booking page beside those answers.

Report results supporting this interpretation

Contains at least 10 images (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzIzhQNAgAvascAR5-YaT-aWaUCrkEHzIQniCQUKHDlH4wlFnkMJckC6tIOSp9CUFHsZw/exec#row=Contains%20at%20least%2010%20images): +255% clicks; +55% citations compared with pages containing no images. The comparison is ten or more images against none; no row measures one image or the one-to-ten range.

No images (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzIzhQNAgAvascAR5-YaT-aWaUCrkEHzIQniCQUKHDlH4wlFnkMJckC6tIOSp9CUFHsZw/exec#row=No%20images): −72% clicks; −33% citations.

Crucial non-obvious information (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzIzhQNAgAvascAR5-YaT-aWaUCrkEHzIQniCQUKHDlH4wlFnkMJckC6tIOSp9CUFHsZw/exec#row=Crucial%20non-obvious%20information): +128% clicks; +154% citations.

## 13Start by bolding the answer or key facts, not by meeting a minimum tag count.

One bold answer line can be useful. Do not force four bold tags onto every page, and do not increase bolding indefinitely because one density test was positive.

Example bold answer:
The course starts on 15 October and costs $300.

Why this rule

At least 4.5 bold or strong tags per 1,000 words: +11% citations; −1% top-five rankings.

Fewer than four bold or strong tags: −7% citations; +17% top-five rankings.

Contains at least 19 bold or strong tags: +3% citations; −22% top-five rankings.

Manual Search 31 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-31) put one bold answer line ahead of three and seven bold tags; Search 32 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-32) put seven and three ahead of none when the one-bold-answer page was absent. View Search 32. (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/screenshots/SEARCH-32-ai-mode.png)

The manual results favor bolding and specifically support the answer line. They do not support a four-tag minimum. A density of 4.5 per 1,000 words and a total below 19 would also conflict on a 5,000-word page.

## 14Use lists for itemized facts, and keep the main content under 132 list entries.

Use a list when the facts are genuinely itemized, such as event date, time, hall and price. Keep the main content below 132 list entries; the long-list group is the group that measured worse in the current data.

Example four-item list:
1. Date: 15 October
2. Time: 8 PM
3. Hall: C
4. Price: $20

Why this rule

132 or more list items in the main content: −64% citations; −6% top-three rankings; −31% top-five rankings compared with fewer than 132 entries. AI Overview clicks and impressions are not measured on this row.

Has an ordered list: +8% citations; +13% AI Overview clicks; −1% top-five rankings.

Zero list items: −19% citations; −24% AI Overview clicks; +19% top-five rankings.

Manual Search 17 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-17) used the numbered-list page's event details; that page carried a short list.

## 15Add one to ten relevant images, and keep important facts in visible text.

Start with one to ten relevant images that clarify the answers; ten is not a tested maximum. Keep every important fact in the visible text as well; alt text is not a place to hide the only copy of an answer. A video used to support “we tested”, “we measured” or “we found” must be indexed by Google, show the claimed test and corroborate at least part of the facts and details stated on the money page. Relevant partial search wording in alt text remains an ordinary-ranking tactic.

Example visible event detail:
“Starts at 8 PM”

Why this rule

Contains at least 10 images: +55% citations; +255% AI Overview clicks; +40% top-three rankings; +11% top-five rankings compared with pages containing no images.

No images: −33% citations; −72% AI Overview clicks; −25% top-three rankings; −7% top-five rankings.

Has an embedded video or iframe: +53% citations; +31% AI Overview clicks; +47% top-five rankings. The row counts any iframe and does not measure whether a video proves a testing claim.

Image alt text: manual-test page y3bx (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#:~:text=y3bx) did not supply the alt-only answer.

Every image has nonempty alt text: −6% citations; −26% top-three rankings; −17% top-five rankings. This is a different condition from placing partial search wording in an alt attribute.

Find the alt-text page in the manual ledger. (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#:~:text=y3bx)

## 15bPublish a YouTube video for each how-to, comparison, why and what search you target.

The AI Overview cites YouTube videos as sources in their own right, more than any other website. Publish a video, or a Short, on YouTube for each target search that starts with how to, why, what, who, when or where, or that compares two things with vs. Put the main topic words and at least half of the search words in the video title. The video does not need to rank in the ordinary Google results. Skip searches about price and searches ending in near me. Embedding the video on the money page does not lift the money page's own citations.

Example:
Target search “how to fix a leaking tap”. YouTube title: “How to Fix a Leaking Tap in 5 Minutes”.
Search to skip:
“plumber near me”.

Why this rule

How often the AI Overview cites a YouTube video, across 8,565 searches that showed one: how to 71.4%; vs 70.0%; why 51.6%; what, who, when, where 44.2%; yes-or-no questions 44.1%; best or top 38.7%; all searches 37.1%; how much or how long 21.0%; price or cost 10.5%; near me 0%. YouTube received 4,104 of those citations, ahead of Reddit (1,970), Facebook (855) and Wikipedia (519).

The cited videos: 65.6% had at least half the search words in the title; 48.4% had the main topic words; 32.0% were Shorts; only 11.3% ranked in the ordinary top 10 for the same search, and 54.3% did not appear in the ordinary results at all.

Embeds a YouTube video player: +3% citations; 0% top-three rankings; +30% top-five rankings. The money page's own citations do not rise from the embed.

Source: the tables “How often the AI answer cites a YouTube video” and “What the cited YouTube videos look like” in the correlation report (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbzIzhQNAgAvascAR5-YaT-aWaUCrkEHzIQniCQUKHDlH4wlFnkMJckC6tIOSp9CUFHsZw/exec). Not yet tested: whether a new video of your own gets cited.

## 15cPublish one to three branded Shorts every day across every active social platform.

Treat every Short as an off-site brand and URL citation. Put the exact brand name and the full website URL in large, readable text inside the video itself; do not rely only on the post caption or profile link. Post each Short across every active social platform, with YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels as the priorities. A visible URL is not an ordinary clickable backlink, but every placement repeatedly associates the brand, domain, person and topic on third-party platforms.

Create a simple cartoon or animated visual with Midjourney, Runway, or an open-source image or video model available to the production agent. Runway's API can automate the video stage. Keep most Shorts between 10 and 30 seconds. Use a clear visual or spoken hook in the first second, cover one idea, move quickly, add readable captions, show the payoff before the ending, and remove introductions or pauses that delay the point. Keep the brand name and URL visible long enough to read, and make the final frame loop cleanly into the opening when possible.

Example production pattern:
Create one short cartoon around a single surprising industry fact. Open immediately with the surprising result. Keep UNDERGROUND SEO UNIVERSITY and underground-seo-university.com readable on screen. Deliver the explanation in under 30 seconds, then publish the same core video to all 11 active social platforms.

Why this rule

Underground SEO University began posting URL-bearing Shorts on August 17, 2026 and increased the program on September 11. Posting one to three Shorts daily across 11 social platforms creates 11 to 33 off-site brand-and-URL placements per day.

Strict brand impressions in Search Console increased from 0.56 per day before August 17 to 1.04 per day from August 17 through September 10 and 1.20 per day from September 11 through September 25.

One YouTube Short published September 11 reached 193,352 views. YouTube and Instagram were the priority platforms in the campaign, while the same brand and domain appeared across all 11 platforms.

The site's average Google position improved from 38.46 during August 29 through September 4 to 20.27 during September 19 through September 25, while weekly impressions remained almost unchanged at 2,034 and 2,028. The sharp improvement began around September 10 through 12.

Observed conclusion: the timing and scale support daily cross-platform, URL-bearing Shorts as a major recurring tactic. The test was not isolated: August Omega Indexer activity and September page changes overlapped, so the Shorts cannot be assigned the entire ranking change by themselves.

## 16Write steps as numbered prose inside paragraph tags.

Write “Step 1 …”, “Step 2 …” as sentences inside paragraph tags instead of turning every procedure into a list. Keep code blocks out of the answer format.

Example:
“Step 1: send the URL. Step 2: receive the audit. Step 3: book the review.”

Why this rule

Has numbered steps written as prose: +61% citations; −23% AI Overview clicks; −38% top-three rankings; −3% top-five rankings.

Has a data table: +12% citations; +17% AI Overview clicks; −19% top-five rankings.

Has a blockquote: +14% citations; +2% AI Overview clicks; −35% top-three rankings; +7% top-five rankings.

Has a code or preformatted block: −7% citations; −61% AI Overview clicks; −33% top-three rankings; −24% top-five rankings.

## 17Keep answers visible; avoid HowTo schema, question headings on pages under 1,500 words, forum quotations and code blocks.

Do not add schema so that AI can read facts that are missing from the visible page. Keep the following out of the money page: HowTo schema, quotations or paraphrases of Reddit and forum users, and code or preformatted blocks. Article schema and Person schema carry their own ordinary-ranking risks; the other schema types have their own separate results.

Keep question subheadings off pages under 1,500 words. On a page of 1,500 words or more, a question subheading is fine when the paragraph directly under it answers in 8 to 60 words and contains a number.

Example heading:
“Coaching fees”
Example visible paragraph:
“The consultation costs $90 and lasts one hour.”
Question subheading allowed on a 2,000-word page:
“How much does SEO coaching cost?” followed at once by “North College charges $300 for six weeks; South College charges $90 per hour.”

Why this rule

HowTo schema: −30% citations; −28% top-three rankings; −7% top-five rankings.

Article schema: −14% citations; −43% top-three rankings; −41% top-five rankings.

Person schema: −14% citations; −51% top-three rankings; −45% top-five rankings.

FAQ schema: +4% citations; −22% top-three rankings; −25% top-five rankings.

Video schema: +15% citations; +16% top-three rankings; +3% top-five rankings.

Three or more JSON-LD blocks: −28% top-three rankings; −33% top-five rankings. Citations are not measured on this row.

Four or more question headings: +26% citations; +83% AI Overview clicks; −21% top-three rankings; −16% top-five rankings.

Question headings split by page length, measured September 25, 2026 on the 20,000-website run, searches containing the business name removed, against pages with no question heading: under 1,500 words +10% citations, −29% top-three rankings, −26% top-five rankings; 1,500 to 3,500 words +12% citations, +35% top-three rankings, +3% top-five rankings. The ranking loss in the row above comes from short pages.

Question heading answered directly underneath in 8 to 60 words with a number: +26% citations; −18% top-three rankings; −1% top-five rankings across all page lengths; on pages of 1,500 to 3,500 words +30% citations, +40% top-three rankings, +20% top-five rankings against pages with no question heading.

Quotes or paraphrases Reddit or forum users: −29% citations; +124% AI Overview clicks; −34% top-three rankings; +25% top-five rankings.

Has a code or preformatted block: −7% citations; −61% AI Overview clicks; −33% top-three rankings; −24% top-five rankings.

## 11bLand the page's semantic score 11 to 20 points over the Goldilocks zone; go further over when the AI Overview is the goal.

The semantic score is the SEO agent's keyword score: every word on the page gets a weight from the search's top-10 competitor pages, the weights of all the words are added up, and the page is ranked against every page on the search. The Goldilocks zone is the top-10 competitors' average score. Pages scoring 11 to 20 points over that average reach Google positions 1 through 5 most often; pages scoring more than 20 points over it get placed in the AI Overview most often, and the first and second sources the AI Overview picks sit 4 points over the average on average. Pages more than 20 points under the average are the ones ranking 51 through 100.

Example:
The top-10 competitors average a semantic score of 55, so the zone is 50 to 60. Write the page to score about 70 for Google positions 1 through 5; write it to 80 or more when the page's job is to be placed in the AI Overview.

Why this rule

Semantic score 11 to 20 points over the Goldilocks zone: +130% AI Overview placements; +94% top-three rankings; +111% top-five rankings.

Semantic score more than 20 points over the Goldilocks zone: +144% AI Overview placements; +88% top-three rankings; +102% top-five rankings.

Semantic score within 5 points of the Goldilocks zone: +118% AI Overview placements; +68% top-three rankings; +90% top-five rankings.

Semantic score 11 to 20 points under the Goldilocks zone: +74% AI Overview placements; +33% top-three rankings; +56% top-five rankings. Every row is compared with pages more than 20 points under the zone, measured September 7, 2026 on Google results 1 through 100 for 1,949 searches, 155,004 pages.

## Who links to which page, with which words

## 18Link to the source inside the sentence where it comes up, and do it for ten or more different websites.

Cite the source in the sentence where it comes up, with a link, and do that for ten or more different non-social websites across the page: the companies, tools, platforms, associations and publishers the page's subject depends on, plus .org bodies and .gov pages where the topic has them. Pages linking to ten or more different websites from their text are cited 33% more and reach Google positions 1 through 5 27% more often than pages with no link to another website in their content. Do not put the links only in a Sources or References list at the end: pages that do that reach Google positions 1 through 5 78% less often. Adding a Sources list on top of the in-text links is neither shown to help nor to hurt. Links to Wikipedia, news outlets, medical-authority pages and Amazon went with fewer citations.

Example:
A page about SEO coaching links, inside its own sentences, to Semrush, HubSpot, Google Search Central, Trustpilot, Ahrefs, Moz, Screaming Frog, Search Engine Land, WordPress.org and Cloudflare where each is discussed: ten different websites.

Why this rule

Main content text links to at least 10 different non-social websites: +33% citations; +39% top-three rankings; +27% top-five rankings.

Links to other websites only in a sources or references list, none in the text: −4% citations; −59% top-three rankings; −78% top-five rankings.

Links to other websites both inside the text and in a sources list: +18% citations; +35% top-three rankings; +8% top-five rankings.

Money page links to at least five different external websites using followed links: +107% citations; +168% top-three rankings; +137% top-five rankings.

Money page links to at least five different external websites using followed or nofollow links: +81% citations; +121% top-three rankings; +107% top-five rankings.

Contains no links to other websites: −38% citations; −32% AI Overview clicks; −46% top-three rankings; −40% top-five rankings.

At least ten non-social outgoing links, compared with none (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/aio-correlation-study/runs/2026-09-03-outbound-follow-status/results.json): +60% citations. Repeated links count separately; this was not a ten-versus-five-website comparison.
The percentages describe the money page containing the outgoing links, not the websites receiving the links.

## 18bGet the business named on the pages that already rank for the same search, and ask for a link while you are there.

List the pages ranking for the target search, with the best-of and top-list pages first. Get the business named on them. A name with no link already helps; a link from the same page helps far more, so ask for the link, and accept the name when the link is refused. A name on a page that does not rank for the search is still positive but weaker, partly because well-known businesses get named everywhere.

Example:
Target search “best seo coach”. The page ranking fourth is titled “10 Best SEO Coaches for 2026”. Ask its editor to add “North College: $300 for a six-week group course”, with a link to northcollege.example.
Name without a link, still counted:
“North College: $300 for a six-week group course.”

Why this rule

Business named without a link by a best-of or top-list page for the same search: +182% citations; +107% top-three rankings; +158% top-five rankings.

Business named without a link by a page ranking 1 to 10 for the same search: +135% citations; −14% top-three rankings; +29% top-five rankings.

Business named without a link by another page ranking for the same search: +82% citations; +155% top-three rankings; +163% top-five rankings.

Business named without a link by at least two other pages ranking for the same search: +57% citations; +34% top-three rankings; +68% top-five rankings. Two naming pages did not beat one.

Linked by another page ranking for the same search: +350% citations; +675% top-three rankings; +516% top-five rankings.

Linked by another page for the same search, compared with named without a link: +147% citations; +203% top-three rankings; +134% top-five rankings.

Each row compares with pages whose business is neither named nor linked by any other page for that search; searches containing the business name are removed. The best-of and ranking-page rows rest on 59 and 71 pages. Not yet measured: the price of a mention against the price of a link, and mentions on Reddit or in press coverage.

## 19Get backlinks pointing directly at the money page, not only at the homepage.

Build direct backlinks to the money page and use the complete search phrase as the clickable text on some of them. Include homepage backlinks alongside the direct money-page backlinks. Build the links in the first hour after the page goes live; the working sequence at the top of this guide states that timing.

Example:
For “best seo coach”, one outside website links to example.com/seo-coach/ using “best SEO coach”; another links to example.com/ using “SEO coach”.

Why this rule

At least one backlink from another website points directly to the money page: +39% citations; +53% top-three rankings; +23% top-five rankings compared with no backlinks to the money page.

Backlink from another website points directly to the money page: +38% citations; +28% top-three rankings; +12% top-five rankings compared with backlinks reaching only the homepage.

Backlink to the money page uses only the complete search phrase: +95% citations; −16% top-three rankings; +57% top-five rankings.

Homepage backlink includes search words in different wording; money page has no direct backlinks: +21% citations; +9% top-five rankings.

## 20Ask for relevant backlink wording, and do not treat generic wording as a penalty.

Use the complete search phrase or relevant partial wording for the strongest backlinks to the money page. Do not remove a legitimate backlink solely because the clickable words are “click here”; the current comparison did not show a generic-wording penalty.

Example:
“Best SEO coach” is the complete phrase; “choosing an SEO coach” is relevant partial wording; “SEO coach” is the exact main entity; “click here” is generic wording.

Why this rule

Backlink to the money page uses only the complete search phrase: +95% citations; −16% top-three rankings; +57% top-five rankings.

Backlink to the money page uses generic wording such as 'click here': +16% citations; +75% top-three rankings; +25% top-five rankings.

Backlink to the money page uses search words within different wording: +8% citations; +51% top-three rankings; +12% top-five rankings.

Backlink to the money page uses only the main entity phrase: −11% citations; +1% top-three rankings; +5% top-five rankings.

Main-entity-phrase backlink lands on the money page itself: −54% citations; +40% top-three rankings; +30% top-five rankings against pages whose main-entity backlinks reach only the homepage.

## 21Do not stop at one linking website because of an assumed citation limit.

Having a direct backlink and having direct backlinks from at least three websites both had positive citation results. Neither test established that further backlinks stop helping after the first one.

Example — three linking websites:
north.example, south.example and west.example each link to example.com/seo-coach.

Why this rule

At least one backlink from another website points directly to the money page: +39% citations; +23% top-five rankings compared with none.

At least three different websites link directly to the money page: +33% citations; +26% top-five rankings compared with fewer than three websites.

The two positive percentages use different comparisons. They do not mean that the second and third backlinks reduce the benefit, or that the first backlink supplies the whole benefit.

## 22Avoid a high share of homepage backlinks whose clickable text is only the domain name.

A high share of bare-domain anchors had a negative result. Generic wording and visible web addresses had different results. A business name is not the same anchor category as a bare domain name.

Business-name text:
“North College”
Bare-domain text:
“example.com”
Web-address text:
“https://example.com/”
Generic text:
“click here”

Why this rule

At least 41.5% of homepage-linking websites use the domain name as clickable text: −22% citations; −40% top-five rankings.

At least 7.2% of homepage-linking websites use generic wording such as 'click here': +6% citations; +63% top-five rankings compared with no more than 1.1%.

At least 10.3% of homepage-linking websites use a web address as clickable text: −3% citations; +15% top-five rankings.

Homepage backlink displays a web address; money page has no direct backlinks: +7% citations; +89% top-five rankings.

The bare-domain warning concerns example.com, not business-name text such as “North College”.

## 23Do not make a zero spam score a link-building target.

Do not hold back relevant backlinks just to preserve a zero spam score. Zero-score money pages had a median of 2 backlinks from 1 website; pages scoring above zero had 23 backlinks from 12 websites.

Example:
The money page’s backlink-profile spam score is 3. Assess the actual backlinks; do not make forcing the score to zero a target.

Why this rule

Money page backlink-profile spam score is zero: −12% citations; −19% top-three rankings; −12% top-five rankings.

Money page backlink-profile spam score is at least 20: +1% citations; −5% top-three rankings; −3% top-five rankings.

At least one backlink to the money page has a spam score of 20 or more: +12% citations; +56% top-three rankings; +29% top-five rankings.

Saved backlink counts (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/aio-correlation-study/runs/2026-09-02-corrected-backlinks/selected_money_pages.jsonl): 2,326 zero-score pages versus 5,320 pages above zero. A higher spam score is not a target either.

## Commercial information and remaining risks

## 24Present service facts like a specification sheet, not a booking request.

State the price, duration, eligibility and included service clearly. Do not add online booking, ordering, purchasing, application, registration or scheduling features as an AI Overview tactic.

Example service facts:
“Duration: six weeks. Lessons: six. Total price: $300. Individual feedback: included.”

Why this rule

Offers online booking, ordering, purchasing, application, registration, or scheduling: −98% impressions; +29% citations; +43% top-three rankings; +21% top-five rankings. The negative impressions result excludes booking and purchase actions from this tactic.

Facts presented like a specification sheet (score 8-10): +51% citations; +46% top-five rankings.

Frames the choice as budget, cheapest, low-cost, affordable, or best value: −2% citations; −3% top-five rankings.

The positive recommendation covers specification-style facts, not booking features or service-page format. A factual price, a “cheapest” claim and an online purchase action are different measurements.

## 25Keep sales copy separate from the ranking page’s answer text.

Move sales pitches, calls to action, award claims and free offers to a separate sales page, such as Contact Us, that is not the page being targeted for rankings. Do not assume one sales call is safe. Keep factual prices and service details in the answer text; budget considerations and discounts are the tested exception, with a positive manual result but a negative impressions correlation.

Placement | Student instruction |

Separate sales page | Put the sales copy on Contact Us or another dedicated sales page, not in the ranking page’s answer text. |

Why this rule

At least two sales calls to action: +35% citations; +5% AI Overview clicks; +23% top-three rankings; +6% top-five rankings; −99% impressions. The sales-call page was used once in 29 recorded manual searches and did not lead the answer.

Claims an award: +41% citations; +39% top-three rankings; +43% top-five rankings; −6% impressions. AI Overview clicks are not measured on this row, and the awards page had a negative manual result.

Offers a free consultation, quote, estimate, assessment, trial, sample, or demo: +23% citations; +9% AI Overview clicks; +2% top-three rankings; −9% top-five rankings; −50% impressions. The free-offer page was not used in the 29-search record.

Manual records: awards, Search 20 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-20); free offer, Search 28 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-28); sales calls to action, Search 29 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-29).

Budget and discounts, Search 48 (https://underground-seo-university.com/api/files/svt4-pages/SVT4-LEDGER.html#run-48): the page containing price-selling and discount wording finished first despite its ticket being listed second. The ledger records appearances in three of five opportunities, not consistent retrieval. Budget wording and discounts occurred together; discounts were not tested separately.

Frames the choice as budget, cheapest, low-cost, affordable, or best value: −54% impressions; −2% citations; 0% top-three rankings; −3% top-five rankings.

Strong advertorial or sales language (score 8-10): −213% impressions; +37% citations; +61% top-three rankings; +17% top-five rankings.

Separating sales copy is the teaching precaution drawn from these results, not proof that every sales phrase hurts. The tests do not establish that one call to action is safe, or that moving sales copy into an image, blocked iframe, SVG or CSS dot font restores performance. ## 26Use a service-page format without a publication dateline for a commercial service.

For a commercial service, present the money page as a service page rather than a dated blog post. Omit the publication or update dateline in this chosen teaching format.

Author byline: keep the author byline, and use an author already known in this field or a neighbouring one. A live test on Josh's own website in September 2026: the pages that kept the byline moved from an average Google position of 53.0 to 35.1, the 10 pages that lost it moved from 57.7 to 42.0, the 5 pages Google recrawled without it on September 20 and 21 gained 3.9 places while the byline pages gained 26.5, and /how-to-choose-seo-coach fell from position 17.2 to 66.1 the day after it was recrawled without the byline. An author unknown in every field, most of all this one, is the one case for leaving the byline off.

Example:
A coaching service page contains the coaching fees, approach, experience and booking details, without a publication-date line.

Why this rule

Service page: +28% citations; −33% AI Overview clicks; +17% top-three rankings; +8% top-five rankings; −93% impressions.

Blog or article page: −16% citations; +90% AI Overview clicks; −23% top-three rankings; −16% top-five rankings; +61% impressions.

Visible publication or update date: +7% citations; +37% AI Overview clicks; −28% top-three rankings; −17% top-five rankings; +42% impressions.

Canonical tag: −1% citations; −28% top-three rankings; −32% top-five rankings.

Gives a specific operating history or says the business is family-run: +14% citations; −30% AI Overview clicks; +7% top-three rankings; −3% top-five rankings; −99% impressions.
The date and article-format exclusions are the chosen format, not findings that clicks or impressions always fall.
